title: Frikadeller
subtitle: Danish Meatballs with Potatoes & Brown Gravy
description: Pan-fried pork and veal meatballs, a true Danish home-cooking staple, served the classic way with boiled potatoes and a rich brown gravy.

sections.name: Frikadeller (Meatballs)
ingredients: ½ lb ground veal (or use all pork, 1½ lb total)
⅓ cup breadcrumbs or all-purpose flour
steps: In a bowl, mix the breadcrumbs (or flour) with the milk and let sit for a few minutes to soften.
Add the ground pork, veal, grated onion, egg, salt, and pepper. Mix well with your hands or a fork until light and well combined — don't overmix.
Cover and refrigerate the mixture for at least 20 minutes; this helps the meatballs hold together and firm up.
With two spoons (or wet hands), shape the mixture into oval patties, about the size of a small egg.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the patties in batches, 5–6 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and cooked through. Keep warm.

sections.name: Boiled Potatoes
steps: Place the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold salted water, and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until fork-tender. Drain well.

sections.name: Brown Gravy (Brun Sovs)
ingredients: 1 tsp soy sauce or browning sauce, for color
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring, for 1–2 minutes until lightly golden (this is a roux).
Gradually whisk in the beef stock, a little at a time, to avoid lumps. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the cream and soy sauce, and simmer for 5–8 minutes until thickened and glossy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

tip: Frying the meatballs in butter (rather than oil) is what gives frikadeller their classic flavor and deep golden color. Don't overcrowd the pan — fry in batches so they brown rather than steam.
